In Progress · Language Grounding & Manipulation
GRASP · Language-Conditioned Sequential Manipulation
Personal research project · Franka Panda · MuJoCo · OWLv2 · asymmetric SAC
Jul 2026 – ongoing
In progress
Working: the randomised kitchen environment, a scripted expert solving 97.3% of 700 episodes, and a camera-only grounding stack measured at 4.7 mm position error and 98% grasp validity. Not working: the learned policy — asymmetric SAC scored 0% across every one of 51 evaluations. Not started: the CBF safety filter and the VLA stage. All numbers re-measured 2026-10-01.
A Franka Panda in a randomised MuJoCo kitchen that takes commands like "pick up all the apples" or "put the carrot in the blue bowl", works out which objects the command refers to, and moves them into the container it names. Nothing is fixed between episodes except the counter and the robot's mounting — object set, placement, container size, colour and shape, and the number of destinations all resample.

The design constraint behind everything: a policy trained on privileged simulator state can never be driven by a camera. It learns to depend on exact poses of occluded objects and perfect labels, and swapping in real perception destroys it silently. So the policy reads Detection objects from a perception interface, never the simulator — and the error of the real detector is measured first, then used as the noise model the policy trains against.

Camera-Only Grounding · 40 Scenes, 166 Objects
Two cameras at 768 px RGB-D, OWLv2 in fp16. Images and a command in; identity, oriented box and a feasible grasp out.
MetricValueReading
Recall154/166 = 93%0 spurious detections
Position error◆ 4.7 mm meanmedian 3.4, p90 7.2
Extent error3.2 mm per axis—
Yaw error, elongated objects4.6° meanmedian 3.4°
Grasp validity◆ 151/154 = 98%against real jaw limits
Label accuracy114/154 = 74%86% excluding the orange fruit
Latency0.65 s per scene2 views — far too slow for an RL loop
The failures are systematic, not random. The model never once told the orange fruit from the orange ball (0/21) — two spheres of near-identical hue separated only by a texture that 768 px does not resolve. It called the red apple a red ball 9 times out of 18. That structure is why the noise model injected during training confuses red apple ↔ red tomato ↔ red ball specifically, rather than scrambling labels uniformly: uniform noise would teach the policy that labels are worthless, while the real confusion structure teaches it to fall back on shape.
End-to-End Referring · The Number That Bounds Everything
RGB-D plus the instruction text against the ground-truth target set. 80 episodes.
Instruction typeCorrect
Specific object — "the carrot"10/1191%
Colour — "the red things"14/1688%
Category — "the apples"6/875%
Everything — "all the items"16/2467%
Kind — "all the produce"9/21◆ 43%
Overall55/8069%
Grounding one named object is nearly solved; resolving a set is not. Accuracy falls as the command requires more objects to be right at once — "all the produce" needs every one of 5–6 detections correct, and a single mislabelled orange sinks the episode. The parser is not the problem: it scores 5000/5000 on held-out templates. This 69% is the real ceiling on the whole system, and it is why the next work is detection quality rather than control.

The Learned Policy Did Not Learn
Asymmetric SAC: actor on noisy camera-derived observations, privileged critic discarded at deployment. 10 envs, replay seeded with 400 expert episodes (48k transitions), 5.1M steps over ~7.3 h.
SignalResultWhat it means
In-training evaluations◆ 0% on all 51never once solved an episode
Entropy temperature α0.031 → ~0exploration switched itself off
Returnsettled at −3.0exactly the −0.01/step time penalty
Re-eval, 50 held-out seeds0/50 solved, grasped in 4/50expert solved 50/50 on the same seeds
Reported as it happened. α decaying to zero while success stays flat is the diagnostic: the critic saw no terminal rewards worth chasing, so it learned that everything is worth about −3, and SAC's automatic temperature tuning correctly concluded there was nothing left to explore for. Seeding the buffer with expert episodes was supposed to prevent exactly this and did not — 48k expert transitions against 5.1M environment steps is a rounding error in the replay buffer. The levers left are curriculum order (start on the reach-only task) and a far higher demo-to-rollout ratio.
Decisions That Took Measurement
Each was a real bug or a wrong answer at some point.
01 A hardcoded workspace clamp made a whole container unreachable. The commanded-TCP box started at x ≥ 0.20, but the secondary bowl sits where x drops to 0.11 — so every object in it was kinematically reachable and forbidden by the environment. Nothing raised an error; it presented as a grasping failure. Worth 5 points of expert success.
02 Grasp detection needed hysteresis. A held capsule rolls and one pad breaks contact for a single frame. With a strict two-finger test every step the carrot was "dropped" mid-lift at exactly its correct 29 mm jaw width. Acquiring needs both fingers; keeping needs one plus proximity. That single change took the expert from 86% to 94%.
03 Tuning on an isolated object was anti-correlated with the real distribution. An isolated grasp sweep picked a −0.012 offset as a clean 100%; on crowded six-object episodes that same offset scores 25%. Not noisy — pointing the wrong way.
04 Contact had to be tuned before anything else was trustworthy. 2 ms steps, implicitfast integrator, elliptic friction cones, impratio 10, condim 6 so rolling friction applies, fingertip friction 1.8/0.08/0.02, and a gripper servo 6× stiffer than the Menagerie default with gainprm rescaled so the control range still means the same thing. Before this, grips crept.
05 Orientation is encoded as cos 2θ / sin 2θ, not θ. A parallel jaw is symmetric under a half turn, so a carrot at +80° and one at −100° need the same wrist angle. The raw angle makes two identical situations look maximally different and puts a discontinuity at ±90°, in the middle of the useful range.
06 Every failure the expert has is a timeout, not a mistake. Over 700 episodes: 0 misplacements, 0 drops. Commands with 1–3 targets are 379/379. Five-target commands are 39/46. The expert is not fragile, it is slow — which is the right failure mode for a benchmark whose job is to prove the task solvable.
My contribution
The whole system: procedurally generated scene and object meshes, the randomised layout sampler, the semantics catalog and instruction parser, the privileged/unprivileged perception boundary, the OWLv2 grounding pipeline through to grasp synthesis, the DLS IK with null-space posture control, the scripted FSM expert, the asymmetric SAC implementation, and the evaluation suite behind every number here.
Upstream
Franka Panda from MuJoCo Menagerie (Apache-2.0) with documented local modifications — the stock gripper is far too weak, stiffened 6×. OWLv2 detector weights, used frozen.
